title: Book One · Chapter 135: A Place at the Window
story:
Mrs Lan can see the street from her front window. Below it is a low space. It is wide enough for a board. Ronan notices it when he comes to return her clips.

“Could pictures go there?” he asks.

Mrs Lan follows his finger.

“My pictures?”

“Street pictures. Only a few.”

She puts the clips in a drawer. “For whom?”

“People will walk past the window. They can stop and look.”

“Then they will stop outside my room.”

Ronan has not thought about that. He only wanted more room for the pictures. Here is a space under the window. He wants to use it. He did not think about people standing outside her room.

“They can look quietly.”

Mrs Lan points to a man outside. He is looking for a coin in his shoe. His bag is on the ground, right in front of her step.

Ronan goes out and asks him to move it. The man says sorry and steps aside. When Ronan comes back, Mrs Lan is sitting down with her book.

“I would like to read this afternoon,” she says.

He nods. He does not ask about the window again.

At supper he tells Mum about his idea. “How many pictures do you have now?” Dad asks. Ronan begins counting. Then he reaches the map and stops counting. He and Leo both made it. Does that count as one picture?

“We need a place people can choose to visit,” Mum says.

“They choose to walk past the window.”

“Mrs Lan does not choose to have visitors there all day.”

Dad reaches for another spoonful of rice. “The classroom was a good size.”

“The classroom needs its wall.”

“Perhaps another room at school.”

Ronan sits very straight. “Could we ask?”

Mum nods. “Ask about a small thing first. Which room? What time? Who will take care of it?”

“What must we do to take care of a room?” he asks Dad. Dad tells him to think about the last person leaving. Who puts the chairs back? Who checks for lost things? Who shuts the window? Ronan thought about happy visitors and his pictures. He did not think about the work at the end. Now he thinks about the empty room. He finds a pencil and adds a little box for the work at the end.

The next morning he writes three questions on a page. He keeps them in his pocket until break. Miss Wu is sitting at her desk, marking exercise books. She asks him to wait. She must finish checking one line first.

He waits. Then he gives her the page.

She reads it and stays quiet. At the last question she puts her pencil down.

“Would this be for our class?”

“Perhaps our families. And the people in the pictures.”

“That needs more than my yes.”

Ronan's shoulders fall.

“But I can ask about a room,” she says. “Not for this week. We need time.”

He has almost asked for tomorrow. He closes his mouth and nods.

Miss Wu asks him to bring a list of the pictures next Monday. She does not ask him for a large show. “Which pictures do you already have?” she asks. Whose pictures are they? Who said yes? May we show all those pictures?

Ronan folds the three questions and puts them back in his pocket. On the walk home he tells Leo. Leo wants a race outside the room too. Ronan writes RACE on the back of the paper, then puts a question mark beside it. Leo has asked about a race. That does not mean they will have one. They can ask Miss Wu first. Then they can make a plan.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：choose＝选择；take care of＝照看、负责；a list of＝一份……清单。

情节提示：clip＝夹子；drawer＝抽屉；empty room＝空房间。

理解：1. Mrs Lan 为什么不适合提供窗下的展示位置？2. Miss Wu 请 Ronan 先带来什么？
